headline: OpenAI reports an automated Linux pipeline that reproduced 1,724 kernel vulnerabilities and developed patches for 948 unique LPEs
summary: OpenAI describes a controlled prototype that scanned selected Linux kernel audit targets using an upcoming cyber model and agent pipeline. In its mid-October run, it reports 2,308 candidate findings, 1,724 dynamically reproduced vulnerabilities, 291 information-leak proofs of concept, 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches corresponding to 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities. OpenAI reports about USD 1.21 million in API-credit cost. OpenAI also reports that human review caught 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 apparent successes in an early run, after which it added an independent path check. The page itself is internally inconsistent: its overview and findings summary say 948 LPE exploits, while the detailed section reports 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches. These remain first-party results from one workflow: independent reproduction, maintainer acceptance of all patches, transfer beyond the tested configurations and generalized security impact are not established.
